column3: Near-verbatim parallel: universal dominion grounds forgiveness and punishment, with forgiving mercy.
Shows punishment being withheld in the presence of seeking forgiveness.
Recasts the same sovereignty-forgiveness-punishment formula within disclosure and accounting of what is hidden.
Places a plea for forgiveness before the day when account is established.
Reinforces that all in heavens and earth belong to God, who suffices as guardian.
Pairs seeking forgiveness and turning back with respite, against the prospect of punishment.
Adds comprehensive encompassing knowledge to the ownership formula.
A concrete confession and granted forgiveness joins the forgiving and merciful names.
Near parallel rejects privileged claims: forgiveness and punishment belong to the owner of all realms.
The rejected contrast does not establish its proposed systemic reading of forgiveness.
Supplies a stated boundary: association is excluded while what is below it may be forgiven.
The rejected night-and-day covering analogy is not support for the focus reading.
Connects divine turning toward people with the forgiving and merciful names.
Links upright turning and seeking forgiveness to exclusive devotion, with warning for association.
Repeats the association boundary already supplied by 4:116, with a distinct description of its gravity.
Names God forgiving and loving, but gives little further context for sovereignty or judgment.
Universal dominion, creation, and power sharpen the source of the focus ayah's authority.
Sets forgiveness alongside honorable provision as part of recompense for faithful action.
Relates forgiveness to good known in hearts and restoration after loss.
Links forgiveness to deferred term while preserving the fixed, unpostponable deadline.
Makes forgiveness an ethic of pardoning and overlooking others while retaining divine mercy.
Keeps remembrance within divine willing and names God worthy of mindfulness and forgiveness.
Holds punishment of hypocrisy and turning toward others together under divine will.
Contrasts haste for evil with forgiveness amid wrongdoing and severe requital.
Divine knowledge of human limitation frames easing, continued duty, and seeking forgiveness.
A direct call to seek forgiveness from the ever-forgiving Lord.
Mercy and forgiveness close a legal accommodation, without developing the focus formula.
Shows seeking forgiveness as a recurring early-morning practice of the righteous.
Provides the punishment side for those holding evil assumptions about God.
Forgiveness and mercy close a legal boundary after an exception for what preceded it.
Near-verbatim parallel joins dominion, punishment, forgiveness, will, and power.
Repentance and reform are the explicit setting for forgiving mercy after a grave accusation.
Universal possession is explicitly tied to recompense for evil and good deeds.
Calls for turning and seeking forgiveness from the forgiving, merciful God.
The same ownership formula ends by returning all matters to God.
Angelic seeking of forgiveness for earth's inhabitants accompanies the forgiving, merciful name.
Connects universal ownership with a command to be mindful, and with divine self-sufficiency.
A plea for forgiveness and entrance into mercy makes the paired terms relational.
Pairs punishment and mercy under divine will, followed by return to God.
Forgiveness and mercy explain delay of earned punishment without cancelling its appointed time.
Universal prostration reinforces dominion but does not address forgiveness or punishment directly.
A believer's plea directly joins forgiveness of sins with protection from the Fire.
Universal willing and unwilling prostration supports dominion only indirectly.
A promised plea for family forgiveness invokes the forgiving, merciful God.
Universal submission is set against many for whom punishment is due, under divine doing.
Links giving to multiplication and forgiveness, but not to the focus's ownership-and-judgment frame.
God's knowledge of heavens, earth, and everything corrects presumptions about religious claims.
A contrary boundary: repeated requests for forgiveness do not obtain it for the defiantly corrupt.
Expands universal possession with exhaustive knowledge, preservation, and permission-bound intercession.
A brief assurance of forgiving mercy after cessation adds little beyond the established pattern.
Knowledge of inner concealment and all realms supports accountable sovereignty.
Repentance before capture is followed by the forgiving, merciful name.
Comprehensive knowledge of movements through earth and heaven is joined to mercy and forgiveness.
The prayer explicitly joins forgiveness and mercy while naming God best in mercy.
Knowledge of the secret in heavens and earth is paired with forgiving mercy.
Forgiving mercy appears as the source of welcome, without further focus terms.
Urges hastening toward forgiveness and a garden, then frames it as divine favor given as He wills.
A ritual command to seek forgiveness adds practice but little to the focus's judgment frame.
Forgiving mercy accompanies exemption from blame for constrained yet sincere people.
Exclusive deity, seeking forgiveness for believers, and God's knowledge of movements belong together.
Universal praise with forbearance and forgiveness supports restraint, but remains indirect.
Exposes a spoken request for forgiveness that conflicts with hidden intent and divine control of harm or benefit.
Forgiving mercy accompanies migration and promised reward, without explaining the focus formula.
A wrongdoing is named and followed by a direct command to seek forgiveness.
Pairs punishment of hypocrisy and association with turning toward believing men and women.
Keeps forgiveness and painful punishment together as two stated divine attributes.
Divine inheritance of heaven and earth gives ownership context, but not forgiveness or punishment.
Gives an explicit sequence of turning, faith, righteous action, and guidance for abundant forgiveness.
No one removes harm or repels favor apart from God; mercy and forgiveness follow divine will.
Forgiveness and great reward follow reverent conduct, with limited relevance to the focus formula.
Creation, pervasive knowledge, presence, and sight support sovereignty only indirectly.
Pardon for certain questions and forgiving forbearance is a narrow legal-discursive instance.
A public commitment against wrongdoing is followed by seeking forgiveness for those who undertake it.
A direct declaration of forgiving mercy, though without the balancing punishment context.
Forgiving mercy accompanies embarkation, but its connection to the focus is only attributive.
A plea for forgiveness occurs with protection from becoming a trial and with divine might and wisdom.
Angels seek forgiveness and protection from punishment for repentant followers, under all-encompassing mercy and knowledge.
Sets forgiveness among the gifts of the garden in sharp contrast to enduring painful punishment.
The creator's summons offers forgiveness and respite to an appointed term.
Praise and seeking forgiveness are joined to God repeatedly accepting return.
Divine inheritance of heavens and earth places amassed wealth and its final consequence under God's knowledge.
A plea for a straying father shows forgiveness requested amid acknowledged deviation.
Forgiving mercy in necessity qualifies a legal prohibition but adds little to the focus formula.
Distinguishes unintentional oaths from what hearts earn, clarifying accountable forgiveness and forbearance.
Divine unrestricted giving counters a claim of constraint, but does not directly treat forgiveness or punishment.
Forgiveness is followed by being made among the honored, giving it a concrete favorable outcome.
Corrects a premature faith claim while retaining forgiveness and mercy for obedient response.
Hope for mercy after faith, migration, and striving is supportive but not specific to the focus judgment.
Permission for private needs is accompanied by seeking forgiveness, joining communal obligation and mercy.
Forgiveness and bounty are promised against fear of poverty, a secondary economic setting.
The day of full exposure declares sole, overpowering kingship, sharpening the focus's dominion claim.
A peaceful separation includes a promise to seek forgiveness for one who rejects the call.
Reward for steadfast belief and practice has no direct forgiveness, punishment, or ownership connection.
Answering God's caller brings forgiveness and protection from painful punishment.
Exclusive worship contrasts with taking religious authorities as lords, illuminating the association boundary.
Forgiveness and honorable reward are announced to those who follow the reminder and fear the Merciful unseen.
The isolated designation of the left-hand companions adds no usable connection to the focus.
An objectionable false utterance is named while pardon and forgiveness remain available.
Commanded obedience and the messenger's clear conveyance lack a direct forgiveness or dominion development.
Distinguishes erasing evil deeds from forgiveness, tying both to mindfulness and great divine favor.
The immediately preceding ayah withholds the decision from the messenger and names turning toward people or punishing them.
Calls believers to hasten toward forgiveness from their Lord, giving the surrounding passage its responsive horizon.
Defines the nearby response to wrongdoing as remembering God and seeking forgiveness without persistence.
Links forgiveness of sins with garden recompense for those who repent rather than persist.
In the same battle setting, divine pardon follows the believers' lapse, alongside forbearance.
A prayer joins forgiveness of sins and evil deeds with protection from the Fire.
Seeks forgiveness, removal of evil deeds, and a good end, making mercy responsive to faith.
The closing prayer distinguishes pardoning, forgiveness, and mercy while seeking relief from burden.
Wrongdoers are directed to seek God and the messenger's forgiveness, finding God accepting and merciful.
One who wrongs self and then seeks forgiveness finds God forgiving and merciful.
Turning back and reform after wrongdoing are met by divine acceptance of repentance.
Wrongdoing in ignorance followed by repentance and reform is met by forgiving mercy.
A direct human plea joins forgiveness and mercy with acknowledgment of loss without them.
After evil deeds, repentance and faith meet a Lord described as forgiving and merciful.
Cessation opens the possibility that what has already passed may be forgiven, while return brings prior consequence.
A contrary boundary states that repeated requests for forgiveness do not secure forgiveness for the hypocrites.
Acknowledged mixed deeds and hope for divine turning add a concrete repentance setting.
God's acceptance of repentance and alms confirms that turning is received by the divine owner.
Forbids seeking forgiveness for those whose association and final fate have become clear.
Joseph's declaration of no blame is followed by an invocation of God as most merciful.
The brothers explicitly ask their father to seek forgiveness for their sins.
God's knowledge of what is within people is followed by forgiveness for those who repeatedly turn back.
Repentance, faith, and righteous action are met by a transformation of evil deeds, extending the focus's mercy side.
Challenges haste for evil before good and calls instead for seeking forgiveness to receive mercy.
Forgiveness and great reward are promised across a comprehensive account of faithful practice.
Addresses those excessive against themselves with the command not to despair of God's mercy and states forgiveness of sins.
Places forgiveness of sin and acceptance of repentance beside severe punishment and abundant bounty.
God accepts repentance from servants and pardons evil deeds while knowing what they do.
Affliction is connected to what hands earned, while God pardons much.
Names the Lord as vast in forgiveness while distinguishing grave sins from lesser lapses.
Mindfulness and faith are linked to a share of mercy, light, and forgiveness.
A communal prayer seeks forgiveness for oneself and earlier believers while rejecting inward rancor.
Divine power to create affection is paired with forgiving mercy across a hostile divide.
Faith and striving are answered with forgiveness of sins and entry into gardens.
Pardoning, overlooking, and forgiving are given as the response to harm within close relations.
Mindfulness brings expiation of evil deeds and magnified reward.
Sincere repentance is linked to expiation of evil deeds and entry into gardens.
